title: Gompertz's law of mortality
summary: Adult death rates rise exponentially with age; countries differ in the level, much less in the rate of ageing.

concepts.label: Life table
concepts.description: A population's death rates by single year of age (Eurostat demo_mlifetable).

children.label: Death rate m(x)
children.description: Deaths per person-year lived at age x.

children.label: Age
children.description: Single years; the last group is open (85+ or 95+).

concepts.label: Gompertz law
concepts.description: m(x) = a·e^(bx): adult mortality rises exponentially with age.

facts.text: Benjamin Gompertz proposed the law in 1825.

children.label: Strehler–Mildvan correlation
children.description: Across populations, a lower level a goes with a steeper slope b.

children.label: Accident hump
children.description: Excess deaths of young adults, mostly men, above the line.

children.label: Mortality deceleration
children.description: The slowing of the rise at the oldest ages (plateau debated).

concepts.label: Cause of death
concepts.description: What the deaths at each age are (Eurostat hlth_cd_aro): would explain the hump and the level.

concepts.label: Biological ageing
concepts.description: The decline of the body's repair and reserve that the slope b measures.
